columns.name: firm
columns.meaning: the registry-derived firm scope this row belongs to; never a typed token

columns.name: account_id
columns.meaning: the custodian account id in the declaration's account form (10-char zero-padded)

columns.name: business_date
columns.meaning: the TRADING day (lib/trading_calendar.py), the performance axis

columns.name: market_value_eod
columns.meaning: V_t -- the custodian's own WHOLE-ACCOUNT value at end of day, cash included (C-VALUE)

columns.name: external_flow
columns.meaning: F_t -- net EXTERNAL flow, capital-in positive, summed over every custodian partition day strictly after t-1 up to and including t (the skipped-day rule, row IRPT_BCKEND-S237)

columns.name: income_received
columns.meaning: income recognised on CASH RECEIPT over the same window as external_flow; a declared departure from GIPS accrual

also_nullable_when.source: computed from Black Diamond values and flows

columns.name: total_return_daily
columns.meaning: the served daily total return; null on NOT_MEASURABLE, where the geometric link BREAKS with a stated gap

columns.name: holdings_price_return
columns.meaning: IRPT_BCKEND's price-only daily return for the same (account, day), the C-GUARD cross-check; null with a reason where absent or not OK

columns.name: holdings_price_return_reason
columns.meaning: why holdings_price_return is null; null when it is present

columns.name: fee_amount
columns.meaning: reserved and unused (C-FEERAIL): always null in method_version 1

columns.name: day_quality
columns.meaning: what this day's number stands on

columns.name: guard_state
columns.meaning: what the holdings-price-return guard DID with this account-day: whether it graded the day at all, and if so whether it agreed. NON-NULL because it is how a consumer tells a guarded number from an unguarded one, and a null there is an unguarded number wearing no label.

columns.name: history_scope
columns.meaning: how much of this account's life the table holds

columns.name: carried_days
columns.meaning: how many custodian partition days the flow window folded in; 1 on an ordinary day, more where a market closure was skipped by the calendar and its flows were carried forward

columns.name: method_version
columns.meaning: the dim_return_method row this figure was produced under

optional_columns.name: source
optional_columns.meaning: where this account-day's return comes from, named in words so a page can state it; one of the values below, and it names the source the return was computed from, not the emitter's code path
values: computed from Black Diamond values and flows
optional_columns.rule: An ABSENT or null source means the table was written before this column existed, or its emitter has not adopted the column yet; a page states NO source for such a table and never infers one from the other columns. A null is never a value of source.

optional_columns.name: flow_claim
optional_columns.meaning: the reason an account-day carries no external flow and no income flow: the row's flows are not built from custodian transactions. Present only where a flow column is null.
optional_columns.reason: vendor-reported return, not built from flows
optional_columns.rule: Required exactly when external_flow or income_received is null, and only where source is orion; a row with a null flow and no claim is invalid, and a row carrying the claim with both flows set is invalid. A consumer that needs flows rejects a row carrying this claim and says so in words; it never treats a null flow as zero.

optional_columns.name: source_account_id
optional_columns.meaning: Orion's integer account id for the account-day, carried beside the custodian account_id so that an Orion row can be joined to Orion's own records
optional_columns.rule: Null for every non-Orion source. For source orion it carries the raw Orion integer id and is REQUIRED when reason_class is UNMAPPED_ACCOUNT, the one case where account_id is null because the account is not a member of account_dim (no id is guessed).

optional_columns.name: row_status
optional_columns.meaning: whether this account-day row carries a value (PRESENT) or carries none (ABSENT, with a reason_class saying why). It answers one question: does this row carry a value.
optional_columns.rule: A null row_status means the row was written by a writer that predates this column; such a row reads PRESENT. An ABSENT row carries a null market value, the flows where the flow rule allows, and a reason_class.

optional_columns.name: reason_class
optional_columns.meaning: why an account-day carries no value: one of eight values, the first that applies in the precedence printed in rule24_record.v041.i_mece_over_a_declared_domain. It answers one question: why not.
optional_columns.rule: Required when row_status is ABSENT and null otherwise: a PRESENT row carries no reason_class, and an ABSENT row without one is invalid.

optional_columns.name: market_value_eod_claim
optional_columns.meaning: for a PRESENT Orion row, whether its end market value (market_value_eod) is the vendor's own end value (measured) or is inferred from the next calendar day's start value (inferred). The claim sits beside the value it describes.
optional_columns.rule: Required on every PRESENT row whose source is orion, and null on an ABSENT row (an ABSENT row carries no market value, so it carries no claim about one). measured is the vendor's own end market value for the day; inferred is an end market value taken from the next calendar day's start value, because the Scope feed carries no end value. A consumer that needs a measured end value rejects a row carrying inferred and says so in words; it never treats inferred as measured.

conditional_columns.name: income_claim
conditional_columns.meaning: the reason an account-day carries no income: the source DOES carry income for the day, but the Black Diamond-computed return method does not separate that income from the account value, so income_received is null and the row carries this claim beside the null.

emitted_when.source: computed from Black Diamond values and flows

required_when.source: computed from Black Diamond values and flows

conditional_columns.rule: Required exactly when income_received is null and the source is 'computed from Black Diamond values and flows'; a row carrying the claim with an income is invalid; a consumer that needs income rejects a row carrying this claim and says so in words; it never treats the null as zero. It sits in conditional_columns, not optional_columns, because one source emits it, so it is outside the hash basis optional_columns.

conditional_columns.name: history_scope_claim
conditional_columns.meaning: the claim beside history_scope: the account-level history_scope is derived by the producer per account, not read from the custodian, so this claim says the value is inferred for the account and never measured
conditional_columns.method: first value day vs source floor
conditional_columns.applies_to: every row written by a producer that derives history_scope per account; a row written before that derivation carries no claim
conditional_columns.rule: history_scope is derived per account, never a constant: PARTIAL_HISTORY when the account's first value day equals the source floor (the earliest balance partition the source holds), so the account existed before the data starts; FULL when the account's first value day is after the source floor, because the whole of its history is held here. The derivation is an inference and the claim says so: history_scope_claim is inferred and is never measured. The column sits in conditional_columns, outside optional_columns, because it is not in the hash basis of optional_columns, so both schema hashes are unchanged. A row without the column makes no claim: it is a partition written before the derivation existed. A 'value day' is a day on which the source holds a row for the account, whatever the row's value: a zero, negative or unreadable balance row counts, so an account with a row on the source floor is PARTIAL_HISTORY.

i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.day_quality: domain: 'what does this account-day's number stand on'. MEASURED (the form computed and the guard agreed) | FLOW_UNRECONCILED (the form and the holdings-plus-income cross-check disagree beyond the measured tolerance) | LARGE_FLOW (the flow is a large share of the base; the value still enters) | NOT_MEASURABLE (no return is computable INSIDE the book -- non-positive prior value, or outside the plausibility band) | SOURCE_LAG (the custodian has not delivered the day). Covered by subtraction: a day is either emitted or not; an emitted day either has a computable base or not (NOT_MEASURABLE); a computable day either reconciles (MEASURED / LARGE_FLOW) or not (FLOW_UNRECONCILED); a day the feed has not delivered is SOURCE_LAG. A day BEFORE the account's first positive value is emitted as NO ROW AT ALL, which is why the domain says 'account-day' and not 'trading day' -- that case is outside the domain rather than a sixth member (ISSUER AMENDMENT 1).
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.return_basis: domain: which arithmetic produced total_return_daily. TWR (the C-METHOD form) | NOT_MEASURABLE (no number is served). HOLDINGS_INCOME_FALLBACK is REMOVED: ruling 17 withdrew the substitution because the holdings return covers the priced, included, LONG basket while total_return_daily covers the whole account, so one cannot stand in for the other. Exhaustive by construction: the column is null iff the value is NOT_MEASURABLE.
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.history_scope: domain: 'how much of this account's life does the table hold'. FULL | PARTIAL_HISTORY. Every round-1 row carries PARTIAL_HISTORY because the emit is a QA thread over six accounts and the all-accounts run is round 2; FULL is declared now so the value exists when that run lands, rather than being added as a schema change then.
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.guard_state: domain: what the holdings guard did with this account-day, over EVERY EMITTED ROW. GRADED_AGREED (it ran inside the comparability domain and the difference was at or below the tolerance) | GRADED_DISAGREED (it ran and the difference exceeded the tolerance) | NOT_GRADED_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN (a usable neighbour return existed but the day fell outside the comparability domain: a short position, an excluded weight above the derived ceiling, a different valuation interval, or a non-OK holdings status) | NOT_GRADED_NO_NEIGHBOUR (no usable neighbour return existed for the account-day at all) | GUARD_NOT_REACHED (the day's verdict was settled before the guard was consulted: no usable V_(t-1), or F_t knowably incomplete through an absent transaction partition, an unvalued in-kind leg or an unparseable cash amount). COVERED BY SUBTRACTION, not by a forward list: every emitted row either reached the guard or did not; a row that reached it either had the day graded or not; graded splits on the tolerance; not-graded splits on whether a usable neighbour existed. There is no sixth state because those four questions are exhaustive and each answer is binary.

rule24_record.ii_same_grain: Every member of day_quality, return_basis and guard_state is an ACCOUNT-DAY property; history_scope is an ACCOUNT property carried on every row of that account and is the one deliberate grain exception, declared here rather than left to be noticed.
rule24_record.iii_intent_coherence: guard_state answers ONE question -- what the guard did -- and nothing else. It deliberately does NOT say whether the day is served (day_quality), which arithmetic ran (return_basis), or why a neighbour was unusable (holdings_price_return_reason). Those are separate axes on the same row, and collapsing any two of them is the defect ruling 18 corrected: FLOW_UNRECONCILED alone could not distinguish the guard disagreeing from the guard never running, and both were served under one label.
rule24_record.iv_state_coherence: WHICH VALUES ONE REMEDY DOES NOT MOVE. Landing the IRPT_BCKEND signed-basket instrument (ruling 20's named enrichment) would move NOT_GRADED_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN toward the GRADED members and would move nothing else. Repairing an upstream delivery gap moves GUARD_NOT_REACHED only. Widening the derived ceiling moves part of NOT_GRADED_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN and cannot touch NOT_GRADED_NO_NEIGHBOUR, which needs a holdings row to exist at all. GRADED_DISAGREED is moved by none of them: it is the one member that reports a real disagreement between two computations rather than an absence, so no coverage remedy can reduce it.

i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.row_status: domain: every account-day of the table's domain is either PRESENT (the row carries a value) or ABSENT (the row carries no value, and a reason_class says why). Both values: PRESENT | ABSENT. Covered by subtraction: a row either carries its value or it does not. A null row_status is not a third value; it reads PRESENT for a writer that predates the column.
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.reason_class: domain: the account-days for which no PRESENT row can be written. the denominator, by subtraction: the account-days of the table's domain less the account-days a PRESENT row is written for. PRECEDENCE: a pair gets exactly ONE reason, the first that applies in this order: UNMAPPED_ACCOUNT (the account is not a member of account_dim) | the feed's own class where the feed gives one, one of NO_GROUP, GROUP_NO_SERIES, NO_START_DATE_AT_SOURCE, SERIES_ENDED_AT_SOURCE | NO_FEED_ROW (the feed holds no row for the account on the day, or holds one with no class of its own) | INCOMPLETE_WINDOW (the day's row is there but a calendar day folded into it is missing) | NO_EOD_VALUE (the day's factor is there but no end market value can be inferred, because the next calendar day's start value is absent). All eight values are named. Overlap test against the feed's four: NO_FEED_ROW is assigned only where the feed gives no class of its own, so it cannot overlap them; INCOMPLETE_WINDOW and NO_EOD_VALUE are assigned only after a feed row that is RETURNED with a factor, and the feed's four are assigned only on rows that are not, so they cannot overlap them either.
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.return_basis: domain: which arithmetic produced total_return_daily. TWR (computed: the C-METHOD form) | NOT_MEASURABLE (no number is served) | VENDOR_REPORTED (a vendor's reported return, not Opal's computation; the Orion feed's own figure). The three are read with day_quality and guard_state on the same row, so VENDOR_REPORTED is never read as a TWR-computed day.

v041.ii_same_grain: Same grain: row_status, reason_class and return_basis are each an ACCOUNT-DAY property, set on every account-day row beside day_quality and guard_state. row_status says whether the account-day carries a value, reason_class says why it does not, and return_basis says whose arithmetic the account-day's number is. The one deliberate account-level exception stays history_scope, as declared in the earlier ii_same_grain record; no account-level column is added here.
v041.iii_intent_coherence: One axis, one intent: row_status answers 'does this row carry a value', reason_class answers 'why not' and is set only where row_status is ABSENT, and return_basis answers 'whose arithmetic produced total_return_daily'. The CTO rulings call the vendor-reported mark return_method: VENDOR_REPORTED. return_method and return_basis are the SAME field under two names: VENDOR_REPORTED is a value of return_basis and no separate return_method column is added, because a second column would put one intent on two columns (rule 24, postulate iii). A later cell may add return_method if the CVO or the CTO asks for it. The producer's internal ABSENT sentinel answers row_status's question and is a recorded overlap, not a column.
v041.iv_state_coherence: WHICH VALUES ONE REMEDY DOES NOT MOVE. Adding an unmapped account to account_dim moves its UNMAPPED_ACCOUNT rows out of that class (to PRESENT, or to the reason the rest of the precedence gives) and moves no NO_GROUP, GROUP_NO_SERIES, NO_START_DATE_AT_SOURCE, SERIES_ENDED_AT_SOURCE, NO_FEED_ROW, INCOMPLETE_WINDOW or NO_EOD_VALUE row. MEASURED, VENDOR_REPORTED and GUARD_NOT_REACHED are read together on an Orion row: day_quality MEASURED is the vendor's own figure, return_basis VENDOR_REPORTED says whose arithmetic it is, and GUARD_NOT_REACHED says no holdings guard graded it. Only a holdings guard run on that day moves GUARD_NOT_REACHED; neither an account_dim change nor a change in the feed's classes moves any of the three.

PRESENT.reading: Collides by NAME only: a capitalised ordinary word in infra authorization and holdings comments, and a provenance state value in infra _scope/maintained_sources.py. No existing table carries a row_status column, so no value is shared with a served schema.

ABSENT.reading: Collides by NAME with three existing meanings: the producer's internal sentinel ABSENT (account_return_daily.py) for a missing factor or method version, the member-source sentinel src == ABSENT (filled_report_values.py), and the capability and projection state ABSENT (infra _scope/global.py); the rest is English in comments. The producer sentinel asks the same question as row_status ABSENT, and that overlap is recorded in rule24_record.v041.iii_intent_coherence.

v041.token_census_finding: COLLISIONS BY NAME ONLY, NOT BY MEANING: PRESENT and ABSENT each carry another meaning elsewhere in the census scope (an infra provenance state, a capability binding, a member-source sentinel), and the producer's ABSENT sentinel asks row_status's own question, which is the one overlap of intent recorded here. i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.market_value_eod_claim: domain: the PRESENT Orion rows, the account-days that carry an end market value from the Scope feed (the denominator: every row with row_status PRESENT and source orion). Both values: measured (the vendor's own end value for the day) | inferred (the end value taken from the next calendar day's start value). Covered by subtraction: a PRESENT Orion end value is either the vendor's own or inferred from the next day's start value, and nothing else can produce one, so the two values cover the denominator with no third member and no null.
i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.return_basis: domain: which arithmetic produced total_return_daily. TWR (the C-METHOD form; for an Orion row the vendor's chained daily factor, a time-weighted return) | NOT_MEASURABLE (no number is served). By subtraction from 0.4.1's printed domain (TWR, NOT_MEASURABLE, VENDOR_REPORTED), VENDOR_REPORTED is removed: it named who computed the figure, which is provenance read from source, not which arithmetic ran. The domain is therefore TWR and NOT_MEASURABLE, and the column is null iff the value is NOT_MEASURABLE.

v042.ii_same_grain: Same grain: market_value_eod and market_value_eod_claim are both ACCOUNT-DAY properties set on the same row. A claim describes the one end value its own row carries, so it has the grain of market_value_eod, and it adds no account-level column; history_scope stays the only account-level exception, as declared in v041.
v042.iii_intent_coherence: Four things, one intent each. market_value_eod_claim answers one question: where the end market value came from (the claim on the end value). flow_claim answers one question: why the flows are null beside a vendor return (the claim beside a null flow). return_basis answers one question: which arithmetic produced total_return_daily (TWR or NOT_MEASURABLE). The provenance, who computed the figure, is read from source on its own axis; it is not a column, and the rulings' return_method is not a column either. None of the axes overlaps another.
v042.iv_state_coherence: WHICH VALUES ONE REMEDY DOES NOT MOVE. When the vendor supplies its own end value for a day, that day's market_value_eod_claim moves from inferred to measured and the market_value_eod it describes becomes the vendor's figure; that remedy moves no flow, no return_basis (which stays TWR on every Orion row), no row_status and no guard_state. VENDOR_REPORTED, which left return_basis, is not a value any row carries: provenance is read from source, and a PRESENT row keeps its claim whatever its return_basis.

market_value_eod_claim.reading: The Scope adapter already writes this field name beside the contract's columns (its row dict, its parquet write through a run-level field constant, and two adapter tests), with the same two values this contract now declares; no contract declared it before this record.

The one name hit, market_value_eod_claim, is the Scope adapter's own field carrying the same two values; the census was measured by git grep -c -w at the census commit, one scan per token.

rule24_record.v043: v043 (IRPT_DASHBD round 147, cell DB-b-282): income_received is nullable where source is 'computed from Black Diamond values and flows'. That method states no separate income basis (its adapter says so: income is inside V through the cash the account holds), so income_received is null on every row of that source. The declaration is the attribute also_nullable_when on income_received, beside nullable_when; nullable_when itself is unchanged and nullable stays false in general, so a null income on any other source is still invalid. No enum member is added: source, flow_claim, reason_class and every other enum are byte-identical, so the word-boundary census of the earlier records is untouched.
rule24_record.v044: v044 (IRPT_DASHBD round 148, cell DB-b-284): income_claim is the claim beside a null income_received where source is 'computed from Black Diamond values and flows', the method that reports no income. The claim has ONE value, absent, with the fixed reason SOURCE_REPORTS_NO_INCOME, and NO OTHER STATE: a row either carries absent or carries no claim, because there is no 'present' value (a number is its own claim). A null income_received without the claim is invalid on that source, and a claim beside an income is invalid on every source. It sits in its own section conditional_columns, not in optional_columns, because one source emits it: the hash basis of optional_columns is untouched, and it adds no enum member, so the word-boundary census of the earlier records is untouched.
rule24_record.v045: v045 (IRPT_DASHBD round 149, cell DB-b-289): the reason of income_claim is renamed from SOURCE_REPORTS_NO_INCOME to RETURN_METHOD_DOES_NOT_SEPARATE_INCOME. The old reason was false: the Cottonwood transaction silver carries non-zero income on 343,256 of 1,096,830 rows, so the SOURCE reports income; it is the Black Diamond-computed return method that does not separate it from the account value. The claim still has ONE value, absent, and NO OTHER STATE, as in v044: a row either carries absent or carries no claim. No enum member, column, optional column, condition or schema hash changes, and the old code stays only in this history and in the earlier entries.
rule24_record.v046: v046 (IRPT_DASHBD round 149, cell DB-b-293): history_scope_claim is the claim beside history_scope. history_scope is an ACCOUNT property, the one grain exception declared in ii_same_grain, and the claim shares that grain exception. Its ONE value is inferred, with NO OTHER STATE: a row either carries inferred or carries no claim, because a derived value that is not measured is labelled inferred, and a row without the column is a partition written before the derivation. Its method is first value day vs source floor: PARTIAL_HISTORY where the account's first value day equals the source floor, FULL where it is after. It adds no enum member, so the word-boundary census of the earlier records is untouched. A 'value day' is a day on which the source holds a row for the account, whatever the row's value: a zero, negative or unreadable balance row counts, so an account with a row on the source floor is PARTIAL_HISTORY.

schema_hash_basis: sha256 over the sorted 'name:type' lines joined by newline, types as the pyarrow type name the producer's ARROW_SCHEMA carries. The check recomputes it against the landed parquet, so contract and artifact cannot drift.
firm_specific_columns: NONE. A firm-specific column is a contract violation (C-SHAPE); no sb_cd, tr_cd or any Schwab code survives into this table -- they live only in the adapter's sources.json.

NEW non-null string column guard_state, 19 columns in all (ruling 18's field: what the holdings guard DID with the account-day).
0.2.0 is the base of this minor bump; the 19 columns, their types and schema_hash are unchanged in 0.3.0.

The successor 0.4.0 makes external_flow and income_received nullable ONLY where source is orion: each carries nullable_when {source: orion, flow_claim: absent}. Both stay nullable false in general, so a null flow on any other source is still invalid.

The successor 0.4.0 adds the OPTIONAL column flow_claim (string, nullable, values [absent], reason 'vendor-reported return, not built from flows') beside source; it is the row's own statement that a flow is absent and why.
The successor 0.4.0 adds the OPTIONAL column source_account_id (int64, nullable), Orion's integer account id, null for every non-Orion source.

The successor 0.4.0 keeps the 19 columns, their names, their types, their meanings and schema_hash unchanged, so every 0.3.0 writer still validates: no existing type changes, and a 0.3.0 row carries no flow_claim and no source_account_id, which are optional.
The successor 0.4.0 adds the top-level source_rules.orion (flows, business_date, account_id) and leaves served_day_rules byte-identical.

schema_hash_control: THE METHOD IS CONTROLLED, not asserted: recomputing it over the same ARROW_SCHEMA with guard_state removed reproduces 0.1.0's published hash b5fa8e4e48bf60ab5bb34cf7e4179ebfdcff8aa9d507ccedbd32eac700222058 exactly. A hash whose method could not reproduce the previous published value would be unverifiable.
producer_pin: data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_reporting/account_return_daily.py -- the 19-field ARROW_SCHEMA this hash is taken from. The producer commit carrying guard_state must land WITH this contract, because the check recomputes the hash against the landed parquet.

source_provenance.orion: vendor-computed: the Orion (Scope) feed's vendor computes the daily return and reports it; the return is not computed inside this book.
source_provenance.computed from Black Diamond values and f: Opal-computed: Opal computes this return from Black Diamond values and flows.
source_provenance.computed from custodian holdings: Opal-computed: Opal computes this return from custodian holdings.

orion.flows: The Orion (Scope) feed carries a vendor-reported return and no flows. Where an Orion flow is absent, external_flow and income_received are null and flow_claim is set to absent beside them, so the row says why. A null flow is never zero: a consumer that needs flows rejects a row carrying flow_claim and says so in words, and never reads the null as 0.
orion.business_date: business_date stays the TRADING day (lib/trading_calendar.py), the performance axis. Each non-trading calendar day's factor compounds (the product of the factors) into the next trading day's factor, and the run manifest states that compounding. A trading day whose own factor is ABSENT stays ABSENT; it is never filled from a neighbouring day.
orion.account_id: account_id is account_dim's own key form (for the Scope feed, Orion's id as a string). source_account_id keeps the raw integer. UNMAPPED_ACCOUNT means the account is not a member of account_dim: its row is ABSENT with reason_class UNMAPPED_ACCOUNT, carries a null account_id and a source_account_id, is never dropped, and its count is recorded in the run record.
orion.return_basis: Orion rows carry return_basis TWR: the Orion feed's chained daily factor is a time-weighted return. Provenance is read from source, not from return_basis: source orion means vendor-computed (see source_provenance). day_quality MEASURED is the vendor's own figure standing on its own, and guard_state GUARD_NOT_REACHED says no holdings guard graded the day, because the vendor return has no holdings guard.

served_day_rules.authority: 1.0.0_SA_CTO~DELL2 msg 7330 (2026-10-13), a clarification that changes no column, no enum and no hash; it states what the served columns already carry for a reader that folds this table into a window.
served_day_rules.graded_disagreed: A GRADED_DISAGREED day serves no number (ruling 17): a window that contains one reads ABSENT, with its reason and the count of such days, and is never compounded around the gap.
served_day_rules.flow_unreconciled: A FLOW_UNRECONCILED day compounds as served, and the window carries the flag with its count ("includes N unreconciled-flow days").
